text: Quine's slogan 'to be is to be the value of a bound variable' expresses which criterion of ontological commitment?
choices: A theory is committed to whatever fundamental entities ground the derivative entities it mentions.
A theory is committed to whatever objects are named by the singular terms it employs.
A theory is committed to exactly those entities that must lie in the range of its bound variables when it is regimented in first-order predicate logic.
A theory is committed only to those entities whose existence is settled internally, once a linguistic framework has been adopted.
explanation: Quine reads commitment off the existential quantifiers of a theory's best first-order regimentation. The tempting distractor is the name-based criterion (option 2): Quine held that singular terms are eliminable via Russellian paraphrase, so commitment is carried by bound variables, not by names.
